newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China denies contingency fund for HK stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: China denies contingency fund for HK stocks - paper.

text.p: A senior Beijing official said he had no knowledge of a Chinese contingency fund to prop up Hong Kong's stock market after Britain returns the territory to China in 1997, a Hong Kong business newspaper said on Monday.
Yu Xiaosong, deputy minister of the State Economic and Trade Commission, told the Economic Journal in Beijing that if the fund existed, relevant departments like his would have known.

Last week, the Beijing-backed Ta Kung Po newspaper in Hong Kong quoted a Chinese Communist Party official as saying China had set up a contingency fund and had made other plans to ensure the stability of Hong Kong's stock market upon the handover.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
China would help Hong Kong's stock market if problems arose, the paper quoted Yu as saying. He did not elaborate.
